properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 18 at 3:39AM MDT until September 18 at 5:00AM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
At 339 AM MDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
thunderstorms producing heavy rain across the warned area. Up to 1.5
inches of rain have fallen. The expected rainfall rate is 0.5 to 1
inch in 1 hour. Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.25 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to
begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges. Rain gauges in the Placitas area
indicate that between 1 and 1.5 inches of rain fell between
Midnight and 2 AM MDT.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Bernalillo, Corrales, Santa Ana Pueblo, Coronado State Monument,
San Felipe Pueblo, Sandia Pueblo, Placitas and Algodones.

This includes the following highways...
Highway 550 between Mile Markers 1 and 2. Interstate 25 between Mile
Markers 236 and 254.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

properties.description:

* WHEN...Until 215 PM MDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Flood waters in Whitetail Canyon will flow into the Rio
Felix overnight into Friday morning. Flooding of low water
crossings along the Rio Felix are expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 17 at 9:29PM EDT by NWS Tampa Bay Ruskin FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

Withlacoochee At US 41 Dunnellon affecting Marion, Levy and Citrus
Counties.

.The Withlacoochee River at Dunnellon has been steadily rising since
July, and on September 15 reached flood stage.  The cause of the high
water along the Withlacoochee River at Dunnellon is due to excessive
hydrilla growth (from the river bottom to the water surface) along a
4.5 mile stretch of river between US 41 and Lake Rousseau.  The
hydrilla is acting like a dam and holding water back, causing water
levels to rise.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Withlacoochee at US 41 Dunnellon.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 28.2 feet, Docks and boat ramps flood along the river
in Citrus and Marion counties.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:45 PM EDT Thursday the stage was 28.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 28.2 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:45 PM EDT Thursday was 28.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 28.2 feet.
- Flood stage is 28.2 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 28.3
feet on 10/05/1965.
- https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.
